title: Buildings and Structures in Cities: Assignment of Headings
summary: Governs the free-floating subdivision --Buildings, structures, etc. under names of cities (introduced 1985). Works on a class of structures in a city get the topical heading subdivided indirectly to the city; [city]--Buildings, structures, etc. is added only when the structures are treated architecturally as physical entities, not institutionally. Headings of the form [city]--[type of structure] were discontinued in 1985.
validation_rules: `--Buildings, structures, etc.` is a free-floating topical subdivision used under names of cities, e.g. `New York (N.Y.)--Buildings, structures, etc.`, `Rome (Italy)--Buildings, structures, etc.` (H 1334.5 Background, sec. 2)

Headings of the form `[city]--[type of structure]` (e.g. `Chicago (Ill.)--Churches`) were discontinued in 1985 and are invalid; use the type-of-structure heading subdivided indirectly to the city instead, e.g. `Skyscrapers--Illinois--Chicago`, `Monuments--Washington (D.C.)`. (H 1334.5 Background, sec. 1)
`[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.` may be followed by a form subdivision, e.g. `Chicago (Ill.)--Buildings, structures, etc.--Guidebooks`. (H 1334.5 sec. 2)
Assign `[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.` in addition to the type-of-structure heading only when the work discusses the structures architecturally (as physical entities). (H 1334.5 sec. 2)
Do not assign `[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.` when the work treats the buildings institutionally (activities or services in them), e.g. discotheques or prison life. (H 1334.5 sec. 3)
For individual named buildings and structures, see H 1334. (H 1334.5 sec. 1)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text:
To a work that discusses collectively a certain class of buildings or other structures in a specific city, assign the appropriate topical heading, subdividing it indirectly to the city level, for example, *Skyscrapers--Illinois--Chicago*; *Monuments--Washington (D.C.)*.

Note: For instructions on the assignment of headings to a work that discusses an individual named building or structure, and for the procedures to establish such headings, see H 1334.

sections.heading: 2. When to assign [city]--Buildings, structures, etc.
sections.text:
If the work discusses the class of structures from the architectural standpoint, that is, if it describes the structures as physical entities, also assign the heading *[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.* Examples:

```
Title: The art deco skyscraper in New York.
650 $0 $a Skyscrapers $z New York (State) $z New York.
650 $0 $a Art deco (Architecture) $z New York (State) $z New
            York.
651 $0 $a New York (N.Y.) $x Buildings, structures, etc.

Title: Chicago churches and synagogues : an architectural pilgrimage.
650 $0 $a Church buildings $z Illinois $z Chicago $v Guidebooks.
650 $0 $a Synagogues $z Illinois $z Chicago $v Guidebooks.
651 $0 $a Chicago (Ill.) $x Buildings, structures, etc.
            $v Guidebooks.

Title: The fountains of Rome.
650 $0 $a Fountains $z Italy $z Rome.
651 $0 $a Rome (Italy) $x Buildings, structures, etc.
```

sections.heading: 3. When to omit [city]--Buildings, structures, etc.
sections.text:
If the work discusses the buildings from the institutional standpoint, that is, if it describes the activities or services performed or occurring in the buildings, rather than describing the buildings as physical entities, do not assign the *[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.* heading. Examples:

```
Title: Night dancin'.
650 $0 $a Discotheques $z New York (State) $z New York.
 [not 651 $0 $a New York (N.Y.) $x Buildings, structures, etc.]

Title: Scenes of prison life in London.
650 $0 $a Prisons $z England $z London.
 [not 651 $0 $a London (England) $x Buildings, structures, etc.]
```
